summary:
Lesotho AgriSense is an app by Prodigy Minds that guides farmers through the whole season using NASA data. It combines NASA POWER weather and soil data, with optional NASA satellite layers through AppEEARS (MODIS vegetation index, SMAP soil moisture and ECOSTRESS surface temperature). For this presentation we use Lesotho, and the farmer chooses a district or enters exact coordinates.
The app shows temperature, rainfall and evapotranspiration trends as graphs and plain text, together with the local crop calendar. It gives a 90-day season outlook that blends NASA history with ECMWF seasonal and 16-day forecasts, and it suggests which crops suit the area.
It compares crop rotations, including the farmer’s current one. The farmer sets priorities such as income, drought safety, water saving and soil health, and the app explains why each rotation is suggested, the evidence, the risks and the gaps. A finance section lets farmers enter their own costs and prices to estimate what they will earn.
An AI assistant, running on a free AI model, answers questions about the farmer’s region using this data, by text or voice. To make the app accessible, a gesture recognizer lets a deaf farmer ask the assistant questions with hand signs, and the answer appears as text, voice and an overlay on the camera view.
The app supports farmer judgement and local expertise. It does not replace them.
details:
Lesotho AgriSense

Smarter Farming. A Greener Lesotho.
Built by Prodigy Minds for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (crop rotation and resilient farming).

What it is

AgriSense is a Python desktop app that turns NASA Earth data into simple farming advice for any of Lesotho’s 10 districts, or for an exact farm location. It supports farmers and local experts. It does not replace them.

What it can do

  • See today’s conditions: a water-stress gauge, simple tiles (plant now? best crop? frost?), charts of rain and water loss, and the local crop calendar.
  • Look ahead 90 days: rainfall chances, a 16-day forecast, when the rains usually start, what to plant and how to prepare for the weather.
  • Compare crop rotations: nine options, including the farmer’s current one. Each shows why it was suggested, the NASA evidence, benefits, gaps and risks. Farmers set their own priorities and try “what if” rainfall and temperature changes.
  • Check the money: farmers enter their own costs and prices to estimate profit.
  • Ask questions: a chat and voice assistant using a free AI model.
  • Use sign language: a camera reads hand signs, so a farmer who cannot speak can ask questions. The answer appears on the camera view in augmented reality. It is not a certified Lesotho Sign Language translator.
  • Extras: a district map, a learning page, a printable farm plan and a short WhatsApp summary.

NASA data used

  • NASA POWER: temperature, rainfall, soil wetness, sunlight, humidity, wind and elevation, from 2001.
  • NASA AppEEARS (optional): MODIS NDVI (plant health), SMAP soil moisture and ECOSTRESS surface temperature.

Also used: ECMWF forecasts through Open-Meteo, FEWS NET and USDA FAS (crop calendar), and FAO (farming zones).

How to run it

  1. Install the requirements: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
  2. Keep the assets folder next to lesotho_agrisense.py.
  3. Start the app: python lesotho_agrisense.py

Optional extras

  • Free AI model: install Ollama from ollama.com, run ollama pull llama3.2, then open Settings > Test AI.
  • Satellite layers: create a free Earthdata account, set EARTHDATA_USER and EARTHDATA_PASS, then tick NDVI or SMAP/ECOSTRESS before fetching.

Limits to know about

  • NASA POWER soil data covers areas of about 50 km, so confirm details on your own field.
  • Crop yields, costs and prices are estimates or placeholders.
  • Seasonal forecasts have limited skill, so the app shows its confidence.
  • The sign recogniser understands still hand shapes only.
  • The satellite layers (SMAP, ECOSTRESS, NDVI) need more field testing.

Screenshots

Add your images to a screenshots folder and link them here.

Credits

The weather and soil data was obtained from the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resource (POWER) Project, funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program. MODIS, SMAP and ECOSTRESS data via NASA AppEEARS (LP DAAC / NSIDC DAAC). Forecasts: ECMWF via Open-Meteo.
